summary: The insertion point and basic crowd-out behavior are correct, but the signature is far too coarse to safely call candidates redundant in this catalog.
issues: Candidates sharing family/DN/PN/connection/bore/execution/actuation can differ materially in catalog evidence that tender queries may require. For example, the current catalog groups hundreds of DN50 PN4 welded manual ball valves despite differences in material, medium, bore, series, thread/configuration, and installation dimensions. The first RRF item can suppress the correct variant.
Direct DN/PN fields override contradictory name/search-text evidence, so inconsistent payloads can be grouped under an incorrect signature.

Tests use synthetic near-identical candidates and do not cover catalog-realistic variants that must remain independently eligible; therefore they do not establish the stated reliable-structure safety claim.
fix_plan: Make grouping genuinely conservative: only collapse candidates whose relevant observable catalog evidence is equivalent, or explicitly return no signature when semantic properties/text conflict or differ.
Validate direct DN/PN against explicit conflicting text rather than blindly preferring the payload field.

Add regression tests with same primary dimensions but differing material, medium, pass type, thread/configuration, and installation dimensions; assert those variants remain in the bounded pool. Then rerun the public measurement.
next_direction: Candidate diversification remains a credible recall experiment, but it needs a much stricter equivalence definition. The catalog has very large coarse structural groups, so coarse signatures are a likely safety regression rather than benign near-duplicate removal.
